title: God’s Plan for Redemption
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner describes how God showed love after the fall (clothing Adam and Eve, the promise in Genesis 3:15), examines how the plan of salvation is fulfilled in Jesus (John 3:16; Romans 5:8; Galatians 4:4-5) and explains why redemption matters (restores people to God, forgiveness, new life).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the consequences of the fall.
floor.question: Name one consequence of the fall.

representations: a bridge drawn across a gap: God and people
a time line from Genesis 3 to Jesus
contexts: forgiving a friend who wronged you

board.do: Draw a gap between God and people, then a bridge.

board.say: Who is the bridge, according to John 3:16?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say Jesus, God's Son.

misconceptions.ask: What did God do for Adam and Eve after the fall?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 3:21: God made garments of skin and clothed them. Love even in judgement.

misconceptions.ask: What does John 3:16 say God gave?
misconceptions.repair: Recite John 3:16 together and underline "his one and only Son".

listen_for: It only helps people become rich
misconceptions.ask: Why is redemption important after the fall?
misconceptions.repair: Explain redeem as "buy back"; read Galatians 4:4-5 and Romans 5:8.

misconceptions.ask: According to Ephesians 2:8-9, how are people saved?
misconceptions.repair: Read Ephesians 2:8-10: saved by grace, created for good works. Works follow, they do not buy.

checks.question: What did God do for Adam and Eve after the fall?
